questions.q: What replaces the VALUES clause in an INSERT INTO ... SELECT statement?
options: A full SELECT query whose result rows become the inserted rows
A second table name listed after INSERT INTO
A CASE expression that generates literal values
Nothing -- VALUES is still required alongside SELECT
questions.explain: Once you write SELECT instead of VALUES, that query's result set becomes the source of every inserted row.

questions.q: How does the target column list match up with the SELECT list in INSERT ... SELECT?
options: By matching column names between source and target
By matching data types only, ignoring order
The SELECT list must list target column names as aliases
By position -- the Nth SELECT column fills the Nth target column
questions.explain: Just like VALUES, the match is purely positional -- source and destination column names don't need to match at all.

questions.q: In 'INSERT INTO dbo.LessonDemo (ProductName, ListPrice, Color) SELECT p.Name, p.ListPrice, p.Color FROM Production.Product AS p WHERE p.Color = 'Red';', what determines which rows get inserted?
options: The IDENTITY column's current value
Whether dbo.LessonDemo already contains a matching row
The WHERE clause inside the SELECT, exactly as it would for a normal query
The order of columns in the CREATE TABLE statement
questions.explain: The SELECT behaves like any other SELECT -- WHERE, JOIN, GROUP BY, and TOP all apply before the rows reach the INSERT.

questions.q: Why is INSERT ... SELECT more efficient than looping through rows and issuing one INSERT per row in application code?
options: It skips writing to the transaction log
It only works on tables without a primary key
SQL Server moves the entire result set in a single set-based operation
SELECT disables constraint checking during the insert
questions.explain: Whether the SELECT returns a handful of rows or thousands, SQL Server copies them all in one statement rather than one round trip per row.

questions.q: Which SELECT features can you use inside an INSERT ... SELECT statement?
options: None -- the SELECT must return every row and column unfiltered
WHERE, JOIN, GROUP BY, and TOP, same as any other SELECT
Only WHERE -- JOIN and GROUP BY are not allowed
Only TOP -- filtering must happen after the insert
questions.explain: The SELECT in INSERT ... SELECT is a normal query, so every clause you already know from reading data is available before the rows are inserted.
